harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Enabled a persistent firewalld configuration on node1 (RHEL 7.9) permitting SSH and TCP/8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound traffic, verified with live connection tests, then completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol (baseline boot_id capture, reboot ack, changed boot_id after reboot, and post-reboot re-verification of firewall persistence and connectivity behavior).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 7.9) and confirmed firewalld was already active/enabled
Captured baseline firewalld state: public zone active with only ssh allowed, default target REJECT via icmp-host-prohibited
Added permanent firewalld rules: --add-port=8080/tcp and --add-service=ssh, then --reload to apply persistently
Verified runtime and permanent firewalld config both show services: dhcpv6-client ssh and ports: 8080/tcp
Inspected generated iptables chains showing ACCEPT for tcp dport 22 and 8080 (NEW,UNTRACKED) with all other traffic falling through to REJECT
Started a real TCP listener on 8080 (python) and performed live connect tests: 8080 connects successfully, unrelated port 9999 is refused (connection refused / icmp-host-prohibited)
Captured baseline boot_id (33b0e84c...) and firewalld active/enabled state before restart
Issued 'shutdown -r now' via nohup so the acknowledgement returned before the SSH connection dropped
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming a new boot_id (7c2a91c8...), proving an actual restart occurred
Post-reboot: verified firewalld is active and enabled, and permanent config still shows ssh + 8080/tcp
Post-reboot: re-ran live connectivity test confirming 8080 accepts connections and port 9999 is refused, proving the firewall rules are enforced after restart
Cleaned up temporary test listener processes

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and TCP 8080
evidence.summary: firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8080/tcp and --add-service=ssh applied and reloaded; both runtime and --permanent listings show services: ssh and ports: 8080/tcp

iptables chain shows only tcp/22 and tcp/8080 ACCEPT in IN_public_allow, with a final REJECT --reject-with icmp-host-prohibited rule; live connect test to port 9999 returns Connection refused while 8080 connects
Baseline boot_id captured, node restarted, new boot_id observed after reconnect, and post-reboot firewall-cmd --list-all still shows ssh + 8080/tcp with firewalld active and enabled

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline boot identity/health
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 33b0e84c-4dd1-406a-8f89-2e8ceca97bd6, uptime since 2026-08-26, firewalld running/active/enabled prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned ack; SSH connection then closed by remote host, confirming the restart command was accepted

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Two polling attempts timed out during reboot, then exec succeeded with boot_id 7c2a91c8-07bc-4b9c-851d-113bfe7c31ed, different from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: recovered service/data state post-restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot uptime shows new boot time (2026-09-29 10:28:40), firewalld active/enabled with persisted ssh+8080/tcp config, and a fresh live connectivity test confirms 8080 accepts connections while port 9999 is refused

attempts.summary: Enabled a persistent firewalld configuration on node1 (RHEL 7.9) permitting SSH and TCP/8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound traffic, verified with live connection tests, then completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol (baseline boot_id capture, reboot ack, changed boot_id after reboot, and post-reboot re-verification of firewall persistence and connectivity behavior).
